Split: yes. The supplied proof bundles four separable obligations that SimonGMT does not provide, plus a short assembly.
(1) Steps 0–1 (chart_divergence): in the chart of graph_chart, T(ω) = ∫_{G⁻¹(E)} div Φ_ω, where Φ_ω is the C¹ compactly supported vector field of G^#ω. This uses the graph facts F1–F3, the injective area formula, extDeriv_pullback and the identity d = div.

(3) Steps 3–4 (pushforward_rep): pushing the De Giorgi boundary through G yields M′, ξ′ and −∫_B⟨Φ_ω, ν⟩ dH^n = ∫_{M′} ξ′(ω) dH^n. It rests on two linear-algebra lemmas, normal_orientation (an oriented frame σ of ν^⊥ with β(σ) = −⟨φ_β, ν⟩) and wedge_orientation (Gram-normalized wedges are unit orientations), and on (4).
(4) area_formula: the area formula on countably rectifiable sets (Simon Ch. 3, 2.1–2.6), which SimonGMT lacks. Simon's printed route also needs the C¹ Approximation Theorem (Ch. 2, 1.5), which is absent. area_formula therefore uses bi-Lipschitz pieces. Three accepted declarations from other branches are reused with byte-identical types: bilipschitz_pieces, tangent_locality and piece_pullback. piece_tangent is new. Its type equals the unaccepted ptd_piece_image_approxTangent_ae of another branch, so it gets a fresh name: unaccepted declarations cannot be reused.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Steps 0 ((F1)–(F3)) and 1 ((1a)–(1e)) of the supplied proof of codim1_rdo_local_unit_representation (Simon 7.5.2 with Ch. 6, 2.35), with the chart data produced by graph_chart taken as hypotheses. The vector field Φ is the field φ_{G^#ω} of step (1e), written with 0-based indices: (φ_β)_j = (−1)^j β(e_{j.succAbove 0}, …, e_{j.succAbove(n−1)}). No departure.

Notation. A := ι* : ℝ^P → ℝ^{n+1}; π(w) := A(w − x); p^⊥(w) := w − x − ιπ(w); K := tsupport ω; F := D ∩ G^{-1}(E); H^{n+1} := μHE[n+1], which on ℝ^{n+1} is Lebesgue measure L^{n+1} = volume. For v ∈ D put c_j(v) := (−1)^j ω(G(v))(DG(v)e_{j.succAbove 0}, …, DG(v)e_{j.succAbove(n−1)}), so Φ = 1_D·Σ_j c_j e_j.

1. (Linear algebra of ι.) Since ι is an isometry, Aι = id (⟨Aιa, b⟩ = ⟨ιa, ιb⟩ = ⟨a, b⟩), and Ah = 0 iff h ⊥ range ι (⟨Ah, b⟩ = ⟨h, ιb⟩). Hence p^⊥(w) ⊥ range ι and w = x + ιπ(w) + p^⊥(w) for every w; also |ιa| = |a|.
2. (The chart map.) G is C² on the open set D. For v ∈ D, u(v) ⊥ range ι, so π(G(v)) = v + Au(v) = v and p^⊥(G(v)) = u(v). Since u maps the open set D into the closed subspace (range ι)^⊥, every difference quotient (u(v + ta) − u(v))/t (t ≠ 0 small) lies in (range ι)^⊥, hence so does Du(v)a; thus A∘Du(v) = 0 and A∘DG(v) = A∘(ι + Du(v)) = id. Consequently: (a) G is injective on D (π∘G = id on D); (b) DG(v) is injective for v ∈ D; (c) DG(v)e_i = ιe_i + Du(v)e_i.
3. ((F1) N ∩ Z = G(D).) If v ∈ D then G(v) ∈ N by hypothesis, and |π(G(v))| = |v| < δ₁, |p^⊥(G(v))| = |u(v)| < δ₂/2 < δ₂, so G(v) ∈ Z. Conversely, let w ∈ N ∩ Z, v := π(w), h := p^⊥(w). Then |v| < δ₁, |h| < δ₂, h ⊥ range ι and x + ιv + h = w ∈ N, so the graph hypothesis gives h = u(v), i.e. w = G(v) with v ∈ D.
4. ((F3) N ∩ Z is relatively closed in Z.) Let w_k ∈ N ∩ Z converge to w ∈ Z. By step 3, w_k = G(π(w_k)). π is continuous, so π(w_k) → π(w), and π(w) ∈ D because w ∈ Z. G is continuous at π(w), hence w = lim G(π(w_k)) = G(π(w)) ∈ N.
5. (C := D ∩ G^{-1}(K) is compact; C = π(K ∩ N).) K is compact (ω has compact support) and K ⊆ Z, so by step 4 the set K ∩ N is closed in K, hence compact, and π(K ∩ N) is compact. If v ∈ C, then G(v) ∈ K ∩ N and v = π(G(v)). If w ∈ K ∩ N, then w ∈ N ∩ Z, so by step 3 w = G(π(w)) with π(w) ∈ D, whence π(w) ∈ C.
6. (Regularity and support of Φ.)
- On the open set D, Φ = Σ_j c_j e_j and every c_j is C¹ there: v ↦ ω(G(v)) is C² on D (ω is C^∞ and G is C² on D), v ↦ DG(v) is C¹ on D (G is C² on the open set D), and (α, b_0, …, b_{n−1}) ↦ α(b_0, …, b_{n−1}) is continuous multilinear.
- If v ∉ C then Φ(v) = 0: either v ∉ D, or G(v) ∉ K, so ω(G(v)) = 0 and all c_j(v) = 0. C is compact, hence closed, so Φ vanishes on the open set ℝ^{n+1} ∖ C.
- The open sets D and ℝ^{n+1} ∖ C cover ℝ^{n+1} (C ⊆ D) and Φ is C¹ on each, so Φ is C¹. Its support lies in the closed set C, hence tsupport Φ ⊆ C ⊆ D is compact.
7. ((1a) E ∩ Z = G(F), F Borel.) If w ∈ E ∩ Z then w ∈ N ∩ Z (E ⊆ N), so w = G(v) with v ∈ D and G(v) ∈ E, i.e. v ∈ F. If v ∈ F then G(v) ∈ E and G(v) ∈ Z by step 3. F is Borel: G is continuous on the open set D, so the map G̃ equal to G on D and to x off D is Borel measurable, and F = D ∩ G̃^{-1}(E).
8. (Localization.) By IsBoundaryOfRegion, T(ω) = ∫_E ξN(w)(dω(w)) dH^{n+1}(w). ω vanishes on the open set ℝ^P ∖ K, hence so does dω (tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω, SimonGMT tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset), and ξN(w)(0) = 0. So the integrand vanishes on E ∖ Z ⊆ E ∖ K, and T(ω) = ∫_{E∩Z} ξN(dω) dH^{n+1} = ∫_{G(F)} ξN(w)(dω(w)) dH^{n+1}(w) by step 7.
9. ((1b) Area formula.) SimonGMT integral_area_formula_of_injective_derivative (Chapter02/WeightedArea.lean), applied to the Borel set F, the map G (differentiable at every point of F ⊆ D with injective derivative, and injective on F, by step 2) and the integrand h(w) := ξN(w)(dω(w)), with finrank ℝ^{n+1} = n + 1 and μHE[n+1] = volume on ℝ^{n+1}, gives ∫_{G(F)} h dH^{n+1} = ∫_F areaJacobianAt G v · h(G(v)) dv. Here areaJacobianAt G v = normDet DG(v) = (det(DG(v)*DG(v)))^{1/2} (areaJacobianAt_eq_sqrt_det_adjoint_comp), and the matrix of DG(v)*DG(v) in the orthonormal basis (e_i) has entries ⟨e_i, DG(v)*DG(v)e_k⟩ = ⟨DG(v)e_i, DG(v)e_k⟩, so areaJacobianAt G v = J(v) by step 2(c).
10. ((1c) Orientation.) For v ∈ F ⊆ D, the orientation hypothesis with α := dω(G(v)) gives J(v)·ξN(G(v))(dω(G(v))) = dω(G(v))(DG(v)e_0, …, DG(v)e_n).
11. ((1d) Pull-back commutes with d.) Let β(y) := ω(G(y))∘DG(y), i.e. β(y)(b_0, …, b_{n−1}) = ω(G(y))(DG(y)b_0, …, DG(y)b_{n−1}). For v ∈ D, ω is differentiable at G(v) and G is C² at v, so Mathlib extDeriv_pullback gives dβ(v) = dω(G(v))∘DG(v). Hence dω(G(v))(DG(v)e_0, …, DG(v)e_n) = dβ(v)(e_0, …, e_n).
12. ((1e) d becomes divergence.) β is C¹ near v ∈ D, so Mathlib extDeriv_apply gives dβ(v)(e_0, …, e_n) = Σ_i (−1)^i D[y ↦ β(y)(e_{i.succAbove 0}, …, e_{i.succAbove(n−1)})](v)e_i = Σ_i Dc_i(v)e_i, because c_i(y) = (−1)^i β(y)(e_{i.succAbove ·}) for y near v in D. On D, Φ = Σ_j c_j e_j, so DΦ(v)e_i = Σ_j (Dc_j(v)e_i)e_j and trace DΦ(v) = Σ_i ⟨DΦ(v)e_i, e_i⟩ = Σ_i Dc_i(v)e_i = dβ(v)(e_0, …, e_n).
13. (Conclusion.) Steps 8–12 give T(ω) = ∫_F J(v)·ξN(G(v))(dω(G(v))) dv = ∫_F trace DΦ(v) dv, and step 6 gives the regularity and support claims. ∎
proof_key_steps: u ⊥ range ι forces Du ⊥ range ι, so π∘G = id and ι*∘DG = id on D: G is an injective C² immersion of D.
The graph property gives N ∩ Z = G(D) and N ∩ Z relatively closed in Z, so D ∩ G⁻¹(tsupport ω) = π(tsupport ω ∩ N) is compact and Φ_ω is C¹ with compact support in D.
T(ω) = ∫_{E∩Z} ξN(dω) dH^{n+1} = ∫_{G(F)} ξN(dω) dH^{n+1} = ∫_F J·ξN(G)(dω∘G) by the injective area formula with Jacobian J = √det Gram(DG e).
The orientation identity and extDeriv_pullback turn J·ξN(G)(dω∘G) into d(G^#ω)(e_0, …, e_n), which extDeriv_apply identifies with div Φ_ω.

Source. It is the mass bound used in step 2 of the supplied proof (through chart_perimeter). The proof below inlines the inequality that the accepted proof takes from dor_ims_unitOrientation_dual.

Proof. Let R = (M_R, θ_R, ξ_R) represent T and let W ⊆ ℝ^P.
1. (Unit orientations do not increase the coefficient norm.) Let ξ be a unit orientation of a subspace: ξ(α) = εα(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all α, with τ orthonormal and ε = ±1. Expand α = Σ_I α_I dx^I over strictly increasing I with α_I = α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)}); then α(τ) = Σ_I α_I det τ_I, where τ_I is the n×n matrix of rows I(1), …, I(n) of [τ_1 … τ_n]. By Cauchy–Schwarz and the Cauchy–Binet formula Σ_I (det τ_I)² = det(τᵀτ) = 1, |ξ(α)| ≤ (Σ_I α_I²)^{1/2} = covectorEuclideanNorm α =: |α|. (For n = 0 the only index is empty and both sides equal |α()|.)
2. Let ω be admissible for M_W(T): ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(z)| ≤ 1 for all z. By R.Represents T, T(ω) = ∫_{M_R} θ_R(z)·ξ_R(z)(ω(z)) dH^n(z).
3. For H^n-a.e. z ∈ M_R, ξ_R(z) is a unit orientation of an n-plane (IMRep.orients), so |ξ_R(z)(ω(z))| ≤ |ω(z)| ≤ 1 by step 1; and ω(z) = 0 off tsupport ω. Hence θ_R ξ_R(ω) ≤ θ_R·1_{tsupport ω} H^n-a.e. on M_R.
4. If the integrand of step 2 is not integrable, the Bochner integral is 0 and ofReal(T(ω)) = 0. Otherwise ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ ∫⁻_{M_R ∩ tsupport ω} θ_R dH^n = μ_R(tsupport ω) ≤ μ_R(W), as tsupport ω is closed and μ_R = (H^n⌞M_R).withDensity θ_R is monotone.
5. Taking the supremum over admissible ω gives M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W). ∎

For admissible ω, T(ω) = ∫_{M_R} θ_R ξ_R(ω) dH^n ≤ ∫⁻_{M_R ∩ tsupport ω} θ_R = μ_R(tsupport ω) ≤ μ_R(W).
Take the supremum over admissible ω.

subproblems.title: G⁻¹(E) has locally finite perimeter in the chart ball (supplied step 2; Simon 6.2.35)

Write D := B_{δ₁}(0) ⊆ ℝ^{n+1}, G(v) := x + ιv + u(v), e_0, …, e_n for the standard basis and J(v) := (det[⟨ιe_i + Du(v)e_i, ιe_k + Du(v)e_k⟩]_{i,k})^{1/2}. Assume: E is Borel, E ⊆ N ∩ U, IsBoundaryOfRegion T E ξN (T(ω) = ∫_E ξN(dω) dH^{n+1} for ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U)), and T is integer multiplicity; δ₁ > 0, δ₂ > 0 and closedBall(x, δ₁ + δ₂) ⊆ U; u is C² on D; for every v ∈ D: u(v) ⊥ range ι, ‖Du(v)‖ ≤ 1, |u(v)| < δ₂/2, G(v) ∈ N, and ξN(G(v))(α)·J(v) = α(ιe_0 + Du(v)e_0, …, ιe_n + Du(v)e_n) for every (n+1)-covector α; and whenever |v| < δ₁, |h| < δ₂, h ⊥ range ι and x + ιv + h ∈ N, then h = u(v). Then F := D ∩ G^{-1}(E) is Borel, and for every compact K ⊆ D there is C ∈ ℝ such that ∫_F trace Dφ dL^{n+1} ≤ C for every C^∞ map φ : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^{n+1} with compact support, tsupport φ ⊆ K and |φ(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Step 2 of the supplied proof (Simon Ch. 6, 2.35). Departure: the bound |ω_φ| ≤ 1 of the supplied proof (Cauchy–Binet invariance of the coefficient norm) is replaced by the crude bound |ω_φ| ≤ c₀ := (n+1)!·P^{n/2}, applied to ω_φ/c₀; as the supplied proof of the grandparent node already remarks, any bound independent of φ suffices. Siblings used: chart_divergence and mass_upper_bound.

Notation. A := ι* (adjoint of ι); π(w) := A(w − x); p^⊥(w) := w − x − ιπ(w); Z := {w : |π(w)| < δ₁, |p^⊥(w)| < δ₂}; DG(v) := derivative of G at v; for an n-form ω on ℝ^P, Φ_ω := 1_D·Σ_{j=0}^{n} (−1)^j ω(G(·))(DG(·)e_{j.succAbove 0}, …, DG(·)e_{j.succAbove(n−1)}) e_j, the field of chart_divergence.

1. (Preliminaries.) F is Borel: G is continuous on the open set D, so F = D ∩ G̃^{-1}(E) for the Borel map G̃ equal to G on D and to x off D. As in chart_divergence step 2: Aι = id, ‖A‖ ≤ 1 (A is the adjoint of an isometry), and for v ∈ D, π(G(v)) = v, p^⊥(G(v)) = u(v) and A∘DG(v) = id (u and Du take values in (range ι)^⊥). Since ι is an isometric embedding of ℝ^{n+1}, P ≥ n + 1 ≥ 1.
2. (The constant.) Fix an IMRep R of T. K̂ := closedBall(x, δ₁ + δ₂) is compact and K̂ ⊆ U, so μ_R(K̂) = R.measure(K̂) = ∫⁻_{M_R ∩ K̂} θ_R dH^n < ∞ (IMRep.locallyIntegrable_mult). Put c₀ := (n+1)!·P^{n/2} ≥ 1 and C := c₀·μ_R(K̂).toReal. This C works for every compact K ⊆ D.
3. (Cut-off.) Choose χ ∈ C^∞(ℝ; [0, 1]) with χ(t) = 1 for t ≤ (δ₂/2)² and χ(t) = 0 for t ≥ (3δ₂/4)² (e.g. built from Real.smoothTransition). Put ζ(w) := χ(|p^⊥(w)|²). ζ is C^∞ (w ↦ |p^⊥(w)|² is a quadratic polynomial) with values in [0, 1].
4. (The test form.) Fix a compact K ⊆ D and a C^∞ map φ with compact support, tsupport φ ⊆ K and |φ| ≤ 1. For p ∈ ℝ^{n+1} let Λ(p) be the n-covector on ℝ^P with Λ(p)(a_0, …, a_{n−1}) := det[p, Aa_0, …, Aa_{n−1}], the (n+1)×(n+1) determinant with these columns: it is multilinear, alternating and continuous in (a_k), and p ↦ Λ(p) is linear. Define ω_φ(w) := ζ(w)·Λ(φ(π(w))). ω_φ is C^∞ (the smooth ζ times the linear Λ composed with the smooth φ∘π).
5. (Support.) If ω_φ(w) ≠ 0, then ζ(w) ≠ 0 and φ(π(w)) ≠ 0, so |p^⊥(w)| < 3δ₂/4 and π(w) ∈ K. Hence tsupport ω_φ ⊆ S := {w : π(w) ∈ K, |p^⊥(w)| ≤ 3δ₂/4}, which is closed and bounded (|w − x| ≤ |ιπ(w)| + |p^⊥(w)| ≤ max_K |·| + 3δ₂/4), so tsupport ω_φ is compact. S ⊆ Z because K ⊆ D. Moreover Z ⊆ K̂ ⊆ U, since |w − x| ≤ |π(w)| + |p^⊥(w)| < δ₁ + δ₂ for w ∈ Z. So ω_φ ∈ 𝒟^n(U) and tsupport ω_φ ⊆ Z.
6. (The pull-back is φ.) Let v ∈ D. Then ζ(G(v)) = χ(|u(v)|²) = 1 because |u(v)| < δ₂/2, π(G(v)) = v and A·DG(v)e_i = e_i. Hence ω_φ(G(v))(DG(v)e_{j.succAbove 0}, …, DG(v)e_{j.succAbove(n−1)}) = det[φ(v), e_{j.succAbove 0}, …, e_{j.succAbove(n−1)}]. Expanding along the first column (Matrix.det_succ_column_zero), only the row-j term survives (every other minor contains the zero row j) and its minor is the identity; so the determinant is (−1)^j φ_j(v), where φ_j := ⟨φ, e_j⟩. Therefore Φ_{ω_φ}(v) = Σ_j (−1)^j(−1)^j φ_j(v)e_j = φ(v). For v ∉ D, Φ_{ω_φ}(v) = 0 = φ(v) because tsupport φ ⊆ K ⊆ D. So Φ_{ω_φ} = φ.
7. (Divergence formula.) chart_divergence applies to ω_φ (all its hypotheses are among ours, and tsupport ω_φ ⊆ Z by step 5). With step 6 it gives T(ω_φ) = ∫_F trace Dφ dL^{n+1}.
8. (Coefficient bound.) For every w and every strictly increasing I = (i_0 < … < i_{n−1}) in {0, …, P − 1}, ω_φ(w)(e_{i_0}, …, e_{i_{n−1}}) = ζ(w)·det M_w with M_w := [φ(π(w)), Ae_{i_0}, …, Ae_{i_{n−1}}]. Every entry of M_w has absolute value ≤ 1 (|φ| ≤ 1 and |Ae_i| ≤ ‖A‖ ≤ 1), so |det M_w| ≤ (n+1)! (Matrix.det_le), and 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1. There are at most P^n maps I : Fin n → Fin P, so covectorEuclideanNorm(ω_φ(w)) ≤ (P^n((n+1)!)²)^{1/2} = c₀.
9. (Mass bound.) ω′ := c₀^{-1}·ω_φ ∈ 𝒟^n(U) satisfies tsupport ω′ ⊆ Z and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω′(w)) = c₀^{-1}covectorEuclideanNorm(ω_φ(w)) ≤ 1, so ω′ ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n Z. Hence ofReal(T(ω′)) ≤ M_Z(T) (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn) ≤ R.measure(Z) (mass_upper_bound) ≤ R.measure(K̂) < ∞. Therefore T(ω′) ≤ μ_R(K̂).toReal, and by linearity of T and step 7, ∫_F trace Dφ = T(ω_φ) = c₀T(ω′) ≤ C. ∎
proof_key_steps: F = D ∩ G⁻¹(E) is Borel because G is continuous on the open ball D.
ω_φ(w) := ζ(w)·det[φ(π(w)), ι*·, …, ι*·] is a test form in 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport in Z ⊆ closedBall(x, δ₁ + δ₂).
ζ∘G = 1, π∘G = id and ι*∘DG = id on D, so Laplace expansion gives Φ_{ω_φ} = φ, and chart_divergence yields T(ω_φ) = ∫_F div φ.
Entrywise determinant bounds give |ω_φ| ≤ c₀ = (n+1)!P^{n/2}; mass_upper_bound for an IMRep R gives ∫_F div φ ≤ c₀·μ_R(closedBall(x, δ₁ + δ₂)) < ∞.

subproblems.title: An orthonormal frame σ of ν^⊥ with β(σ) = −⟨φ_β, ν⟩ for all n-covectors β
subproblems.statement: Let n ≥ 1 and ν ∈ ℝ^{n+1} with |ν| = 1, and let e_0, …, e_n be the standard basis of ℝ^{n+1} and j.succAbove the increasing enumeration of {0, …, n} ∖ {j}. Then there is an orthonormal family σ = (σ_0, …, σ_{n−1}) in ℝ^{n+1} with span{σ_k} = (span{ν})^⊥ such that every n-covector β on ℝ^{n+1} satisfies β(σ_0, …, σ_{n−1}) = −Σ_{j=0}^{n} (−1)^j β(e_{j.succAbove 0}, …, e_{j.succAbove(n−1)})·⟨e_j, ν⟩.

Source. The orientation computation of step 3 of the supplied proof: 'If σ is orthonormal in ν(v)^⊥ with det[ν(v), σ] = −1, expanding det[φ_β, σ] gives β(σ) = −⟨φ_β, ν(v)⟩', with 0-based indices and φ_β := Σ_j (−1)^j β(e_{j.succAbove 0}, …, e_{j.succAbove(n−1)}) e_j.

1. (Oriented frame.) Q := (span{ν})^⊥ has dimension n. Choose an orthonormal basis τ_0, …, τ_{n−1} of Q (e.g. stdOrthonormalBasis of Q reindexed by Fin n). Then (ν, τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) is an orthonormal basis of ℝ^{n+1}, so the matrix W with these columns is orthogonal and det W = ±1. If det W = +1, replace τ_0 by −τ_0 (possible since n ≥ 1); the family stays orthonormal with the same span and det W changes sign. Call the result σ; thus (†) det[ν, σ_0, …, σ_{n−1}] = −1.
2. (Coordinates of β.) For j ∈ {0, …, n} put b_j := β(e_{j.succAbove 0}, …, e_{j.succAbove(n−1)}). For a_0, …, a_{n−1} ∈ ℝ^{n+1} let M_j(a) be the n×n matrix with entries ⟨e_{j.succAbove k}, a_l⟩ (row k, column l). Then β(a) = Σ_j b_j det M_j(a). Indeed, by multilinearity β(a) = Σ_s (Π_l ⟨e_{s(l)}, a_l⟩)·β(e_{s(0)}, …, e_{s(n−1)}) over all maps s : {0, …, n−1} → {0, …, n}. Terms with s non-injective vanish (β is alternating). An injective s misses exactly one index j and equals j.succAbove∘ρ for a unique permutation ρ of {0, …, n−1}, and then β(e_s) = sign(ρ)·b_j. Summing over ρ for fixed j gives b_j det M_j(a).
3. (Laplace expansion.) For w ∈ ℝ^{n+1}, expanding the (n+1)×(n+1) determinant of [w, a_0, …, a_{n−1}] along its first column (Matrix.det_succ_column_zero) gives Σ_j (−1)^j⟨e_j, w⟩ det M_j(a).
4. Put φ := Σ_j (−1)^j b_j e_j. By steps 2 and 3, det[φ, a_0, …, a_{n−1}] = Σ_j (−1)^j(−1)^j b_j det M_j(a) = β(a) for all a.
5. Take a := σ. Write φ = ⟨φ, ν⟩ν + Σ_k ⟨φ, σ_k⟩σ_k (the orthonormal basis of step 1). The determinant is linear in its first column and vanishes when two columns are equal, so det[φ, σ] = ⟨φ, ν⟩·det[ν, σ] = −⟨φ, ν⟩ by (†). Hence β(σ) = −⟨φ, ν⟩ = −Σ_j (−1)^j b_j⟨e_j, ν⟩. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take an orthonormal basis σ of ν^⊥ and flip σ_0 if necessary so that det[ν, σ] = −1 (possible as n ≥ 1).
Multilinear expansion and Laplace expansion along the first column give β(a) = det[φ_β, a] with φ_β := Σ_j (−1)^j β(e_{j.succAbove ·}) e_j.
Decomposing φ_β in the basis (ν, σ) gives β(σ) = ⟨φ_β, ν⟩det[ν, σ] = −⟨φ_β, ν⟩.

subproblems.title: The Gram-normalized wedge of linearly independent vectors is a unit orientation of their span
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let a_0, …, a_{n−1} ∈ ℝ^P be linearly independent, with Gram matrix Γ := (⟨a_i, a_k⟩)_{i,k}. Then det Γ > 0, and every n-vector ξ ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) with ξ(α) = (det Γ)^{−1/2}·α(a_0, …, a_{n−1}) for all n-covectors α is a unit orientation of span{a_0, …, a_{n−1}}, i.e. there is an orthonormal basis τ of this span with ξ(α) = α(τ) for all α or ξ(α) = −α(τ) for all α.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (a : Fin n → Euclid P), LinearIndependent ℝ a → 0 < Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin n => inner ℝ (a i) (a j)) ∧ ∀ ξ : MultiVector P n, (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, ξ α = (Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin n => inner ℝ (a i) (a j))))⁻¹ * α a) → IsUnitOrientationOf ξ (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range a))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. The Gram–Schmidt argument cited in step 4(d) of the supplied proof ('By Gram–Schmidt (as in graph_chart (6c)), each ξ′(w) is a unit orientation'), stated for an arbitrary independent family.

1. V := span{a_0, …, a_{n−1}} has dimension n. Choose an orthonormal basis τ_0, …, τ_{n−1} of V indexed by Fin n (e.g. stdOrthonormalBasis of V reindexed, or gramSchmidtNormed applied to a).
2. Let R be the n×n matrix R_{kl} := ⟨τ_k, a_l⟩. Since a_l ∈ V, a_l = Σ_k R_{kl}τ_k; R is invertible because the a_l are independent.
3. (Gram determinant.) ⟨a_i, a_k⟩ = Σ_{p,q} R_{pi}R_{qk}⟨τ_p, τ_q⟩ = (RᵀR)_{ik}. So det Γ = det(R)² > 0 and (det Γ)^{1/2} = |det R|.
4. (Expansion.) For every n-covector α on ℝ^P, α(a_0, …, a_{n−1}) = det R·α(τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}). Indeed, the restriction of α to V is an alternating n-form on the n-dimensional space V, so it equals α(τ)·det_τ (Mathlib AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det for the basis τ of V), and det_τ(a) = det R. (Equivalently, expand multilinearly as in normal_orientation, step 2.)
5. Hence ξ(α) = (det R/|det R|)·α(τ) = εα(τ) with ε ∈ {1, −1} independent of α. τ is orthonormal with span V, so ξ is a unit orientation of V. For n = 0 the families are empty, Γ is the empty matrix with det Γ = 1, V = 0 and ξ(α) = α(τ). ∎
proof_key_steps: Write a = τR with τ an orthonormal basis of V = span(a) and R_{kl} = ⟨τ_k, a_l⟩ invertible.
Gram(a) = RᵀR, so det Gram(a) = det(R)² > 0.
α(a) = det R·α(τ) for every n-covector α, so ξ = sign(det R)·(α ↦ α(τ)) is a unit orientation of V.

subproblems.title: A Borel countably n-rectifiable set is, up to a null set, a disjoint union of bi-Lipschitz Borel pieces (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let M ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel and countably n-rectifiable. Then there are Lipschitz maps F_i : ℝ^n → ℝ^P, Borel sets B_i ⊆ ℝ^n and constants m_i > 0 (i ∈ ℕ) such that m_i|a − a'| ≤ |F_i(a) − F_i(a')| for a, a' ∈ B_i, F_i is differentiable with injective derivative at every point of B_i, each F_i(B_i) is a Borel subset of M, the sets F_i(B_i) are pairwise disjoint, and H^n(M ∖ ⋃_i F_i(B_i)) = 0.

Source. It supplies the bi-Lipschitz decomposition used in step 1 of area_formula (in place of Simon's C¹-submanifold decomposition, Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 and Remark 1.3). The proof recorded for the accepted node is reproduced below.

Notation: E := ℝ^P; H^n := μHE[n] (on ℝ^n it equals Lebesgue measure, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).
1. Rectifiable cover. By CountablyRectifiable n M there are M₀ ⊆ E with H^n(M₀) = 0 and Lipschitz maps F_j : ℝ^n → E (j ∈ ℕ) with M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n).
2. Regular sets. Let G_j := {a ∈ ℝ^n : F_j is differentiable at a and DF_j(a) is injective} (SimonGMT areaRegularSet F_j). G_j is Borel (SimonGMT measurableSet_areaRegularSet) and H^n(F_j(ℝ^n ∖ G_j)) = 0 (SimonGMT area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero with s = univ; finrank ℝ ℝ^n = n).
3. Coercivity constant and radius. For an injective linear A : ℝ^n → E choose m(A) > 0 with (†) |Ah| ≥ m(A)|h| for all h ∈ ℝ^n: if n ≥ 1 take m(A) := min{|Ah| : |h| = 1} (the unit sphere is compact and nonempty and h ↦ |Ah| is continuous and positive on it; for h ≠ 0 apply this to h/|h|; h = 0 is trivial); if n = 0 take m(A) := 1 (the only vector is h = 0). (Alternatively m(A) := 1/K for K > 0 with AntilipschitzWith K A from Mathlib LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith, valid in every dimension.) Define r : (ℝ^n →L[ℝ] E) → ℝ≥0 by r(A) := m(A)/2 if A is injective and r(A) := 1 otherwise. Then r(A) ≠ 0 for every A.
4. Partition. For each j apply Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt to f := F_j, s := G_j, f' := fderiv ℝ F_j (for a ∈ G_j, F_j is differentiable at a, so HasFDerivWithinAt F_j (DF_j(a)) G_j a) and the radius r of step 3 (rpos holds). It gives pairwise disjoint measurable sets t_{j,k} ⊆ ℝ^n (k ∈ ℕ) with G_j ⊆ ⋃_k t_{j,k}, and continuous linear maps A_{j,k} with ApproximatesLinearOn F_j A_{j,k} (G_j ∩ t_{j,k}) (r(A_{j,k})), i.e. |F_j(a) − F_j(a') − A_{j,k}(a − a')| ≤ r(A_{j,k})|a − a'| for a, a' ∈ G_j ∩ t_{j,k}; and if G_j ≠ ∅ then A_{j,k} = DF_j(y) for some y ∈ G_j.
5. Bi-Lipschitz pieces. Put D_{j,k} := G_j ∩ t_{j,k} (Borel) and ρ_{j,k} := r(A_{j,k}) > 0. Claim: |F_j(a) − F_j(a')| ≥ ρ_{j,k}|a − a'| for a, a' ∈ D_{j,k}. If D_{j,k} = ∅ this is vacuous. Otherwise G_j ≠ ∅, so A := A_{j,k} = DF_j(y) with y ∈ G_j is injective and ρ_{j,k} = m(A)/2; by step 4 and (†), |F_j(a) − F_j(a')| ≥ |A(a − a')| − (m(A)/2)|a − a'| ≥ (m(A)/2)|a − a'|. In particular F_j is injective on D_{j,k}, and F_j is differentiable with injective derivative at every point of D_{j,k} ⊆ G_j.
6. Enumeration. Let i ↦ (j(i), k(i)) be the bijection ℕ → ℕ × ℕ (Nat.unpair). Put F_i := F_{j(i)}, D_i := D_{j(i),k(i)}, m_i := ρ_{j(i),k(i)} > 0, and N_i := F_i(D_i). F_i is continuous, D_i Borel and F_i injective on D_i, so N_i is Borel by the Lusin–Souslin theorem (Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn).
7. Disjoint pieces. Define B_i := D_i ∩ F_i^{-1}(M ∖ ⋃_{i'<i} N_{i'}). B_i is Borel (F_i continuous; M and the N_{i'} Borel) and F_i(B_i) = (N_i ∩ M) ∖ ⋃_{i'<i} N_{i'} =: P_i, which is Borel and contained in M. Since B_i ⊆ D_i, the lower bound m_i|a − a'| ≤ |F_i(a) − F_i(a')| and the differentiability/injectivity of DF_i hold on B_i, and F_i is Lipschitz. If i' < i then P_{i'} ⊆ N_{i'} and P_i ∩ N_{i'} = ∅, so the P_i are pairwise disjoint. (This is the recursive definition B_i := (D_i ∩ F_i^{-1}(M)) ∖ F_i^{-1}(⋃_{i'<i} F_{i'}(B_{i'})) in closed form: by induction ⋃_{i'<i} F_{i'}(B_{i'}) = M ∩ ⋃_{i'<i} N_{i'}.)
8. Null remainder. Let x ∈ M ∖ (M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n ∖ G_j)). By step 1, x = F_j(a) for some j and a, and a ∈ G_j. Then a ∈ t_{j,k} for some k, so a ∈ D_i for the index i with (j(i), k(i)) = (j, k), and x ∈ N_i ∩ M. If i₀ is the least index with x ∈ N_{i₀}, then x ∈ P_{i₀}. Hence M ∖ ⋃_i F_i(B_i) ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n ∖ G_j), a countable union of H^n-null sets (steps 1–2), so H^n(M ∖ ⋃_i F_i(B_i)) = 0.
9. n = 0 and n > P need no separate treatment: for n = 0 every A is injective, m(A) = 1, r(A) = 1/2, every map ℝ^0 → E is differentiable with injective derivative (G_j = ℝ^0), and each D_i ⊆ ℝ^0 has at most one point; for n > P no linear map ℝ^n → E is injective, so all G_j are empty, all B_i = ∅, and step 8 says H^n(M) = 0. (Imports: areaRegularSet and its lemmas live in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLipschitz, which the submission may import; the frozen statement does not use it.)
proof_key_steps: Cover M by M₀ ∪ ⋃F_j(ℝ^n) and remove the null images F_j(ℝ^n ∖ G_j) of the non-regular points.
Radius r(A) := m(A)/2 for injective A (m(A) a coercivity constant, 1 when n = 0), r(A) := 1 otherwise, so r(A) ≠ 0 for all A.
Mathlib's partition theorem gives pieces G_j ∩ t_{j,k} on which F_j is bi-Lipschitz with lower constant r(A_{j,k}).
Enumerate the pieces over ℕ; their images are Borel by Lusin–Souslin.
B_i := D_i ∩ F_i^{-1}(M ∖ ⋃_{i'<i} F_{i'}(D_{i'})) yields disjoint Borel images in M covering M up to a null set.

subproblems.title: Locality of approximate tangent spaces for nested sets (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2); Ch. 1, 3.6) (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open and let A ⊆ B ⊆ U be Borel sets with H^n(B ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U. Then for H^n-a.e. x ∈ A and every linear subspace Q of ℝ^P: B has approximate tangent space Q at x (Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4; HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q) if and only if A has approximate tangent space Q at x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U A B : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet B → A ⊆ B → B ⊆ U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (B ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict A), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Reused accepted declaration Submission.regcomp_approx_tangent_locality with byte-identical frozen type (node root.regular_components_are_minimizing-a1.approx_tangent_locality-a1); fresh compilation of its candidate commit 048ff2b9 prints only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. It is the locality of approximate tangent spaces (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2)) used in step 2(b) of area_formula. The proof recorded for the accepted node is reproduced below.

Notation: η_{x,λ}(z) = λ^{−1}(z − x); H^n = μHE[n]; HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q means dim Q = n and ∫_{η_{x,λ}(M)} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as λ ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P). Simon's H^n (SimonGMT simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n) and μHE[n] are positive constant multiples of μH[n], so they have the same null sets; only this is used.

1. (Vanishing density of B ∖ A at a.e. point of A.) For j ≥ 1 let V_j := {z ∈ U : |z| < j, dist(z, ℝ^P ∖ U) > 1/j} (V_j := ball(0, j) if U = ℝ^P). Each V_j is open with compact closure in U, and ⋃_j V_j = U. A'_j := (B ∖ A) ∩ V_j is Borel with H^n(A'_j) ≤ H^n(B ∩ closure(V_j)) < ∞. By the Upper Density Theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6, applied to the Borel regular measure H^n and the set A'_j of finite measure; SimonGMT Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_6 and simon_remark_3_7_hausdorff), Θ^{*n}(H^n, A'_j, x) := limsup_{ρ↓0} H^n(A'_j ∩ B_ρ(x))/(ω_n ρ^n) = 0 for H^n-a.e. x ∈ ℝ^P ∖ A'_j. Let N₀ := ⋃_j {x ∈ A ∩ V_j : Θ^{*n}(H^n, A'_j, x) ≠ 0}; since A ∩ V_j ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ A'_j, N₀ is H^n-null. For x ∈ A ∖ N₀ choose j with x ∈ V_j; for small ρ, B_ρ(x) ⊆ V_j and so H^n((B ∖ A) ∩ B_ρ(x)) = H^n(A'_j ∩ B_ρ(x)). (The density quotient may be taken with closed or open balls: H^n(A'_j ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ H^n(A'_j ∩ closedBall(x, ρ)).) Hence
 (†) lim_{ρ↓0} ρ^{−n} H^n((B ∖ A) ∩ B_ρ(x)) = 0 for every x ∈ A ∖ N₀.

2. (Comparison of blow-ups.) Fix x ∈ A ∖ N₀ and f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f ⊆ B_R(0) (R > 0), and choose λ₀ > 0 with closedBall(x, λ₀R) ⊆ U. For 0 < λ < λ₀ the map η := η_{x,λ} is an injective affine similarity, so η(B) is the disjoint union of the Borel sets η(A) and η(B ∖ A), and for Borel S ⊆ ℝ^P, H^n(η(S) ∩ B_R(0)) = λ^{−n} H^n(S ∩ B_{λR}(x)) (translation invariance and H^n(cS) = |c|^n H^n(S)); for S ⊆ B this is finite because closedBall(x, λR) is a compact subset of U. Hence f is integrable on η(B), η(A) and η(B ∖ A),
 ∫_{η(B)} f dH^n − ∫_{η(A)} f dH^n = ∫_{η(B∖A)} f dH^n, and
 |∫_{η(B∖A)} f dH^n| ≤ sup|f| · λ^{−n} H^n((B ∖ A) ∩ B_{λR}(x)) = sup|f| · R^n (λR)^{−n} H^n((B ∖ A) ∩ B_{λR}(x)) → 0 as λ ↓ 0, by (†).

3. (Conclusion.) Therefore, for x ∈ A ∖ N₀ and every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), ∫_{η_{x,λ}(B)} f dH^n converges to a limit L as λ ↓ 0 if and only if ∫_{η_{x,λ}(A)} f dH^n converges to L. The requirement dim Q = n is the same on both sides. So for every x ∈ A ∖ N₀ and every Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q ⟺ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q. Since A is Borel and N₀ is H^n-null, this holds for μHE[n].restrict A-almost every x.
proof_key_steps: Exhaust U by open V_j ⊂⊂ U and apply the Upper Density Theorem to (B ∖ A) ∩ V_j: ρ^{−n}H^n((B ∖ A) ∩ B_ρ(x)) → 0 for H^n-a.e. x ∈ A.
At such x the blow-ups of B and of A differ by η_{x,λ}(B ∖ A), whose H^n-measure inside B_R(0) is λ^{−n}H^n((B ∖ A) ∩ B_{λR}(x)) → 0.
Hence the limits in Definition 1.4 coincide for B and A.

subproblems.title: Borel image and null-set pullback along a bi-Lipschitz piece (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let F : ℝ^n → ℝ^P be L-Lipschitz, B ⊆ ℝ^n Borel and m > 0 with m|a − a'| ≤ |F(a) − F(a')| for all a, a' ∈ B. Then F(B) is Borel. Moreover, for every predicate p on ℝ^P that holds H^n⌞F(B)-a.e. (H^n = μHE[n]), p(F(b)) holds for Lebesgue-a.e. b ∈ B, i.e. (volume.restrict B)-a.e.

Source. Reused accepted declaration Submission.ptd_piece_image_measurable_ae_pullback with byte-identical frozen type (node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.diffeo_pushforward-a1.piece_tangent_density-a1.piece_pullback-a1); fresh compilation of its candidate commit bed5b849 prints only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. It transfers H^n-a.e. statements on a bi-Lipschitz piece F(B) to Lebesgue-a.e. statements on B, in step 2(d) of area_formula. The proof recorded for the accepted node is reproduced below.

Notation: E := ℝ^P; H^n := μHE[n] on E and on ℝ^n; λ := volume on ℝ^n. On ℝ^n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), μHE[n] = λ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).
1. F is injective on B. If a, a' ∈ B and F(a) = F(a'), then m|a − a'| ≤ |F(a) − F(a')| = 0, and m > 0 gives a = a'.
2. F(B) is Borel. F is continuous (Lipschitz), ℝ^n is Polish, B is Borel and F is injective on B. So F(B) is Borel by the Lusin–Souslin theorem (MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn).
3. Inverse map. Let G := Function.invFunOn F B : E → ℝ^n. For y ∈ F(B), G(y) ∈ B and F(G(y)) = y (invFunOn_pos). For y, y' ∈ F(B), m|G(y) − G(y')| ≤ |F(G(y)) − F(G(y'))| = |y − y'|. So G is m^{-1}-Lipschitz on F(B), that is, LipschitzOnWith (Real.toNNReal m^{-1}) G (F '' B). The Lipschitz image bound (SimonGMT Chapter02 euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn, valid between any two metric spaces with their Borel σ-algebras) gives μHE[n](G(S)) ≤ (m^{-1})^n μHE[n](S) for every S ⊆ F(B).
4. Pullback. Let p be a predicate on E with p(y) for H^n⌞F(B)-a.e. y.
- F(B) is measurable by step 2. So, by ae_restrict_iff', H^n-a.e. y satisfies y ∈ F(B) → p(y). That is, S := {y : y ∈ F(B) ∧ ¬p(y)} is H^n-null.
- Let T := {b : b ∈ B ∧ ¬p(F(b))}. If b ∈ T then y := F(b) ∈ S. Also G(y) ∈ B and F(G(y)) = F(b), so G(y) = b by step 1. Hence T ⊆ G(S).
- By step 3 and μHE[n] = λ on ℝ^n, λ(T) ≤ μHE[n](G(S)) ≤ (m^{-1})^n · 0 = 0.
- Since B is measurable, ae_restrict_iff' turns λ(T) = 0 into: p(F(b)) holds for (volume.restrict B)-a.e. b. ∎
For n = 0 every power is 1 and the argument is unchanged.
proof_key_steps: The lower bound m|a − a'| ≤ |F a − F a'| makes F injective on B.
Lusin–Souslin: F(B) is Borel.
G := invFunOn F B is m⁻¹-Lipschitz on F(B); the Lipschitz image bound gives μHE[n](G(S)) ≤ m^{-n} μHE[n](S).
The bad parameters {b ∈ B : ¬p(F b)} lie in G of the H^n-null bad image set; μHE[n] = volume on ℝ^n, and ae_restrict_iff' concludes.

subproblems.title: A bi-Lipschitz piece F(B) has approximate tangent space range DF(b) at F(b) for a.e. b ∈ B
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, F : ℝ^n → ℝ^P L-Lipschitz, B ⊆ ℝ^n Borel and m > 0 with m|a − a′| ≤ |F(a) − F(a′)| for all a, a′ ∈ B, and suppose F is differentiable with injective derivative DF(b) at every b ∈ B. Then for Lebesgue-almost every b ∈ B, range DF(b) is the approximate tangent space of F(B) at F(b) in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, 1.4 (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (F(B)) (F(b)) (range DF(b))).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (F : Euclid n → Euclid P) (B : Set (Euclid n)) (L : NNReal) (m : ℝ), LipschitzWith L F → MeasurableSet B → 0 < m → (∀ a ∈ B, ∀ a' ∈ B, m * ‖a - a'‖ ≤ ‖F a - F a'‖) → (∀ a ∈ B, DifferentiableAt ℝ F a ∧ Injective (fderiv ℝ F a)) → ∀ᵐ b ∂(volume.restrict B), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (F '' B) (F b) (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ F b : Euclid n →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. The blow-up argument of the proof of Simon Ch. 3, 1.6 '⇒' (chapter-03.txt lines 109–144), applied to one bi-Lipschitz Lipschitz piece instead of a piece of a C¹ submanifold. It provides the identification T_vB = (tangent plane of the piece) that the area formula on rectifiable sets (Ch. 3, 2.1–2.4) needs in step 4(e) of the supplied proof; it is used by the sibling area_formula. The same statement occurs, not yet accepted, as ptd_piece_image_approxTangent_ae in another branch.

Notation. H^n := μHE[n]; on ℝ^n it equals Lebesgue measure λ = volume. J(a) := areaJacobianAt F a = normDet DF(a). η_{y,r}(z) := r^{-1}(z − y) (SimonGMT blowUpMap). A := F(B). HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S y Q means: dim Q = n and ∫_{η_{y,r}(S)} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as r → 0⁺ for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P).

0. Preliminaries.
(a) F is injective on B (if F(a) = F(a′) then m|a − a′| ≤ 0) and continuous, so A is Borel (Lusin–Souslin, MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn).
(b) J is Borel (SimonGMT measurable_areaJacobianAt) and 0 ≤ J ≤ L^n: ‖DF(a)‖ ≤ L, and for a linear T, normDet T·λ(B_1(0)) = H^n(T(B_1(0))) ≤ ‖T‖^n λ(B_1(0)) (Mathlib LinearMap.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_eq_normDet_mul_volume and SimonGMT euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn). In particular J is locally integrable.
(c) Area formula: ∫_A g dH^n = ∫_B J(a)·g(F(a)) dλ(a) for every g : ℝ^P → ℝ (SimonGMT integral_area_formula_of_injective_derivative with s := B, using 0(a), the hypotheses on DF, finrank ℝ^n = n and μHE[n] = λ on ℝ^n; no integrability is needed).
(d) Scaling: η_{y,r} (r > 0) is a similarity with ratio r^{-1}, so H^n(η_{y,r}(S)) = r^{-n}H^n(S) (translation invariance and homogeneity of H^n: Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image), and hence ∫_{η_{y,r}(S)} g dH^n = r^{-n}∫_S g(η_{y,r}(z)) dH^n(z) for Borel S and every g (η_{y,r} is a measurable embedding; MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map).
1. (Good points.) By the Lebesgue differentiation theorem for λ (Mathlib IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub applied to the locally integrable function g₀ := 1_B·J), for λ-a.e. b ∈ ℝ^n,
 (β) r^{-n}∫_{B̄_r(b)} |1_B(a)J(a) − 1_B(b)J(b)| dλ(a) → 0 as r → 0⁺.
Fix b ∈ B satisfying (β); λ-a.e. b ∈ B does. Put y := F(b), Λ := DF(b) (injective by hypothesis) and Q := range Λ, so dim Q = n.
2. (Coercivity.) Λ is injective on the finite-dimensional ℝ^n, so there is κ > 0 with |Λc| ≥ κ|c| for all c.
3. (Rescaled formula.) Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) and R > 0 with f = 0 outside B_R(0); let M := sup|f|. For r > 0 put Φ_r(c) := (F(b + rc) − F(b))/r. By 0(d), 0(c) and the substitution a = b + rc (λ is translation invariant and λ(r·S) = r^n λ(S)):
 I(r) := ∫_{η_{y,r}(A)} f dH^n = r^{-n}∫_A f(η_{y,r}(z)) dH^n(z) = r^{-n}∫_B J(a) f((F(a) − y)/r) dλ(a) = ∫_{ℝ^n} 1_B(b + rc)J(b + rc) f(Φ_r(c)) dλ(c).
4. (Localization.) If b + rc ∈ B and f(Φ_r(c)) ≠ 0, then |Φ_r(c)| < R, and since b, b + rc ∈ B, m·r|c| ≤ |F(b + rc) − F(b)| < rR, so |c| < R/m. If f(Λc) ≠ 0 then |Λc| < R, so |c| < R/κ. Let ρ := max(R/m, R/κ) and D_ρ := B̄_ρ(0). Both c ↦ 1_B(b + rc)J(b + rc)f(Φ_r(c)) and c ↦ J(b)f(Λc) vanish outside D_ρ.
5. (Convergence.) For c ∈ D_ρ, |1_B(b + rc)J(b + rc)f(Φ_r(c)) − J(b)f(Λc)| ≤ M|1_B(b + rc)J(b + rc) − J(b)| + J(b)|f(Φ_r(c)) − f(Λc)|.
(i) Since b ∈ B, ∫_{D_ρ} |1_B(b + rc)J(b + rc) − J(b)| dλ(c) = r^{-n}∫_{B̄_{rρ}(b)} |1_B J − 1_B(b)J(b)| dλ = ρ^n·(rρ)^{-n}∫_{B̄_{rρ}(b)} |1_B J − 1_B(b)J(b)| dλ → 0 by (β).
(ii) F is differentiable at b: for θ > 0 there is s_θ > 0 with |F(b + h) − F(b) − Λh| ≤ θ|h| for |h| < s_θ. For 0 < r < s_θ/ρ and c ∈ D_ρ this gives |Φ_r(c) − Λc| ≤ θρ. So Φ_r → Λ uniformly on D_ρ; f is uniformly continuous, hence sup_{D_ρ}|f∘Φ_r − f∘Λ| → 0 and ∫_{D_ρ} J(b)|f(Φ_r(c)) − f(Λc)| dλ(c) ≤ J(b)λ(D_ρ)·sup_{D_ρ}|f∘Φ_r − f∘Λ| → 0.
By step 4 the integrands vanish off D_ρ, so I(r) → I_∞ := ∫_{ℝ^n} J(b)f(Λc) dλ(c) as r → 0⁺.
6. (Identification.) Λ is injective and J(b) = normDet Λ, so by the linear area formula (Mathlib LinearMap.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_eq_normDet_mul_volume: H^n(Λ(S)) = normDet Λ·λ(S), i.e. H^n⌞Q is the image of normDet Λ·λ under the injective map Λ) ∫_Q f dH^n = ∫_{ℝ^n} normDet Λ·f(Λc) dλ(c) = I_∞.
7. (Conclusion.) For every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), ∫_{η_{F(b),r}(F(B))} f dH^n → ∫_{range DF(b)} f dH^n as r → 0⁺, and dim range DF(b) = n. So HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (F(B)) (F(b)) (range DF(b)) holds at every b ∈ B satisfying (β), that is, for (volume.restrict B)-a.e. b. ∎
proof_key_steps: Area formula for the injective piece and scaling of H^n: ∫_{η_{F(b),r}(F(B))} f dH^n = ∫ 1_B(b+rc)J_F(b+rc) f((F(b+rc) − F(b))/r) dc.
The bi-Lipschitz lower bound and injectivity of DF(b) confine both integrands to a fixed ball.
At Lebesgue points b ∈ B of 1_B·J_F, differentiability of F at b gives convergence to ∫ J_F(b) f(DF(b)c) dc.
The linear area formula identifies the limit with ∫_{range DF(b)} f dH^n.

subproblems.title: Area formula on a countably rectifiable set for an injective C¹ immersion (Simon Ch. 3, 2.1–2.6)
subproblems.statement: Let m, d, P ∈ ℕ with m ≥ 1, D ⊆ ℝ^d open and G : ℝ^d → ℝ^P C¹ on D, injective on D, with DG(v) injective for every v ∈ D. Let B ⊆ D be Borel and countably m-rectifiable with H^m(B ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ D (H^m = μHE[m]), and let Q assign to each v ∈ ℝ^d a linear subspace Q(v) such that, for H^m-a.e. v ∈ B, Q(v) is the approximate tangent space of B at v (Simon Ch. 3, 1.4). Then G(B) is countably m-rectifiable, H^m(G(B ∩ K)) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ D, and there is a Borel J : ℝ^d → [0, ∞) such that: for H^m-a.e. v ∈ B and every orthonormal family σ = (σ_0, …, σ_{m−1}) spanning Q(v), J(v) = (det[⟨DG(v)σ_i, DG(v)σ_k⟩]_{i,k})^{1/2}; ∫⁻_{G(B)} g dH^m = ∫⁻_B J(v)g(G(v)) dH^m(v) for every g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞]; and ∫_{G(B)} f dH^m = ∫_B J(v)f(G(v)) dH^m(v) for every f : ℝ^P → ℝ (Bochner integrals).

Source. The area formula on a countably rectifiable set, Simon Ch. 3, 2.1–2.6 (chapter-03.txt lines 330–420: 2.4 and its consequences 2.5–2.6 for injective maps), as used in step 4(e) of the supplied proof ('apply the area formula on the rectifiable set B′ (Simon Ch. 3, 2.3–2.6) … the Jacobian along T_vB′ = T_vB = ν(v)^⊥'). Departure from the printed proof: Simon decomposes M into pieces of C¹ submanifolds (Lemma 1.2 and Remark 1.3, which need the C¹ Approximation Theorem of Ch. 2, 1.5) and uses T_xM = T_xN_j (Remark 1.5(2)). Here B is decomposed into bi-Lipschitz Lipschitz pieces by the accepted sibling bilipschitz_pieces, and the tangent identification on each piece comes from piece_tangent, tangent_locality and piece_pullback. The area formula on the pieces, the Jacobian chain rule and the summation follow Simon. Siblings used: bilipschitz_pieces, tangent_locality, piece_pullback, piece_tangent.

Notation. H^m := μHE[m]; on ℝ^m it equals Lebesgue measure λ = volume. For a linear map Λ on ℝ^m, normDet Λ := (det(Λ*Λ))^{1/2} = (det[⟨Λe_k, Λe_l⟩])^{1/2} (SimonGMT areaJacobianAt f a = normDet Df(a)). For a linear Γ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P and σ : Fin m → ℝ^d, Gr(Γ, σ) := det[⟨Γσ_i, Γσ_k⟩] ≥ 0 (a Gram determinant).

0. (Local Lipschitz bounds; first two conclusions.)
(a) G is Lipschitz on every compact K ⊆ D. For v₀ ∈ D choose r > 0 with closedBall(v₀, 2r) ⊆ D; DG is continuous on D, hence bounded by some L₀ on this compact convex ball, and the mean value inequality makes G L₀-Lipschitz on it. Cover K by finitely many balls B(v_k, r_k) of this kind (constants L_k), and let ρ := min_k r_k, L := max_k L_k and M_K := sup_K|G| < ∞. If v, v′ ∈ K and |v − v′| < ρ, then v ∈ B(v_k, r_k) for some k, v′ ∈ B(v_k, 2r_k), and |G(v) − G(v′)| ≤ L|v − v′|. If |v − v′| ≥ ρ, then |G(v) − G(v′)| ≤ 2M_K ≤ (2M_K/ρ)|v − v′|.
(b) Hence H^m(G(S)) ≤ L_K^m H^m(S) for S ⊆ K (SimonGMT euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn). With the compact exhaustion K_j := {v ∈ ℝ^d : |v| ≤ j, dist(v, ℝ^d ∖ D) ≥ 1/j} of D (K_j := closedBall(0, j) if D = ℝ^d), H^m(G(S)) = 0 for every H^m-null S ⊆ D.
(c) For compact K ⊆ D, H^m(G(B ∩ K)) ≤ L_K^m H^m(B ∩ K) < ∞. This is the second conclusion.
(d) By countable rectifiability, B ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_k range Ψ_k with H^m(M₀) = 0 and Ψ_k : ℝ^m → ℝ^d Lipschitz. For each j, G|_{K_j} is Lipschitz and extends to a Lipschitz map G̃_j : ℝ^d → ℝ^P (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_finite_dimension). Then G(B ∩ K_j) = G̃_j(B ∩ K_j) ⊆ G̃_j(M₀) ∪ ⋃_k range(G̃_j∘Ψ_k), where H^m(G̃_j(M₀)) = 0 and each G̃_j∘Ψ_k is Lipschitz. So G(B ∩ K_j) is countably m-rectifiable, and so is G(B) = ⋃_j G(B ∩ K_j) (SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_iUnion, CountablyRectifiable.mono, countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero, countablyRectifiable_range). This is the first conclusion.
1. (Pieces.) bilipschitz_pieces (with P := d, n := m, M := B) gives Lipschitz F_i : ℝ^m → ℝ^d, Borel B_i ⊆ ℝ^m and c_i > 0 (i ∈ ℕ) with c_i|a − a′| ≤ |F_i(a) − F_i(a′)| on B_i, F_i differentiable with DF_i(b) injective at every b ∈ B_i, the sets A_i := F_i(B_i) Borel, contained in B and pairwise disjoint, and N := B ∖ ⋃_i A_i H^m-null. F_i is injective on B_i. As A_i ⊆ B ⊆ D and G is C¹ on the open set D, G∘F_i is differentiable at every b ∈ B_i with D(G∘F_i)(b) = DG(F_i(b))∘DF_i(b), which is injective; and G∘F_i is injective on B_i.
2. (Tangent identification.) Fix i. Claim: for λ-a.e. b ∈ B_i, Q(F_i(b)) = range DF_i(b).
(a) piece_tangent (F := F_i, B := B_i, m := c_i): for λ-a.e. b ∈ B_i, A_i has approximate tangent space range DF_i(b) at F_i(b).
(b) tangent_locality (U := D, A := A_i, B := B; A_i ⊆ B ⊆ D are Borel and H^m(B ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ D): for H^m-a.e. x ∈ A_i and every subspace Q′, B has approximate tangent space Q′ at x iff A_i has.
(c) The hypothesis holds H^m⌞B-a.e., hence H^m⌞A_i-a.e. (A_i ⊆ B): for H^m-a.e. x ∈ A_i, B has approximate tangent space Q(x) at x.
(d) piece_pullback (F := F_i, B := B_i, m := c_i) transfers the H^m⌞A_i-a.e. statement (b) ∧ (c) at x = F_i(b) to λ-a.e. b ∈ B_i.
(e) For b satisfying (a), (b) and (c): B has approximate tangent space Q(F_i(b)) at F_i(b), hence so does A_i by (b); A_i also has range DF_i(b) by (a); by uniqueness (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), Q(F_i(b)) = range DF_i(b).
3. (Jacobian chain rule.) Let Λ : ℝ^m → ℝ^d be injective linear, Γ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P linear and σ : Fin m → ℝ^d orthonormal with span σ = range Λ. Then normDet(ΓΛ) = Gr(Γ, σ)^{1/2}·normDet Λ. Proof: let R_{kl} := ⟨σ_k, Λe_l⟩, so Λe_l = Σ_k R_{kl}σ_k. Then [⟨Λe_k, Λe_l⟩] = RᵀR and [⟨ΓΛe_k, ΓΛe_l⟩] = Rᵀ[⟨Γσ_a, Γσ_b⟩]R. Taking determinants, (normDet Λ)² = det(R)² and (normDet ΓΛ)² = det(R)²·Gr(Γ, σ); take nonnegative square roots.
4. (Definition of J.) For b ∈ B_i let j_i(b) := normDet D(G∘F_i)(b)/normDet DF_i(b); the denominator is > 0 as DF_i(b) is injective. F_i restricted to B_i is a measurable embedding (Mathlib ContinuousOn.measurableEmbedding: F_i continuous and injective on the Borel set B_i), so ψ_i := (F_i|_{B_i})^{-1} : A_i → B_i is Borel; b ↦ normDet DF_i(b) and b ↦ normDet D(G∘F_i)(b) are Borel (SimonGMT measurable_areaJacobianAt). Define J(v) := j_i(ψ_i(v)) for v ∈ A_i and J(v) := 0 for v ∉ ⋃_i A_i; this is well defined because the A_i are disjoint. J is Borel, J ≥ 0, and (‡) J(F_i(b))·normDet DF_i(b) = normDet D(G∘F_i)(b) for every b ∈ B_i.
5. (Third conclusion.) For b as in step 2(e), Q(F_i(b)) = range DF_i(b), so for every orthonormal σ spanning Q(F_i(b)), step 3 with Λ := DF_i(b) and Γ := DG(F_i(b)) gives J(F_i(b)) = normDet(DG(F_i(b))DF_i(b))/normDet DF_i(b) = Gr(DG(F_i(b)), σ)^{1/2}. The exceptional b form a λ-null set E_i ⊆ B_i, and F_i(E_i) is H^m-null (F_i is Lipschitz; SimonGMT euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn with μHE[m] = λ on ℝ^m). So the Gram identity holds for H^m-a.e. v ∈ A_i, for every i, hence for H^m-a.e. v ∈ B = N ∪ ⋃_i A_i.
6. (Fourth conclusion.) Fix g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] (no measurability needed).
(a) (One piece.) SimonGMT weighted_area_formula_of_injective_derivative (finrank ℝ^m = m, any weight), applied first to G∘F_i on B_i (step 1) and then to F_i on B_i with the weight h(v) := ofReal(J(v))·g(G(v)), together with (‡) and ofReal(st) = ofReal(s)·ofReal(t) for s, t ≥ 0, gives
 ∫⁻_{G(A_i)} g dH^m = ∫⁻_{B_i} ofReal(normDet D(G∘F_i)(b))·g(G(F_i(b))) db = ∫⁻_{B_i} ofReal(normDet DF_i(b))·h(F_i(b)) db = ∫⁻_{A_i} ofReal(J(v))·g(G(v)) dH^m(v),
 using G(A_i) = (G∘F_i)(B_i).
(b) (Summation.) The sets G(A_i) are Borel (Lusin–Souslin: A_i Borel, G continuous and injective on D) and pairwise disjoint (G injective on D), G(B) = G(N) ∪ ⋃_i G(A_i), and H^m(G(N)) = 0 by 0(b). Hence H^m⌞G(B) = Σ_i H^m⌞G(A_i) and H^m⌞B = Σ_i H^m⌞A_i as measures, and lintegrals of arbitrary functions are additive over such sums (lintegral_sum_measure). So ∫⁻_{G(B)} g = Σ_i ∫⁻_{G(A_i)} g = Σ_i ∫⁻_{A_i} ofReal(J)·(g∘G) = ∫⁻_B ofReal(J)·(g∘G).
7. (Fifth conclusion.) Let μ_J := (H^m⌞B).withDensity(ofReal∘J). By step 6 with g := 1_T for Borel T ⊆ ℝ^P, H^m(G(B) ∩ T) = μ_J(B ∩ G^{-1}(T)). G restricted to the Borel set B is a measurable embedding (ContinuousOn.measurableEmbedding), so H^m⌞G(B) is the image of μ_J (carried by B) under G|_B. MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map gives ∫_{G(B)} f dH^m = ∫ f(G(v)) dμ_J(v) for every f : ℝ^P → ℝ, and integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul (Borel density J ≥ 0) gives ∫ f(G(v)) dμ_J(v) = ∫_B J(v)f(G(v)) dH^m(v). Both identities hold for arbitrary f (non-integrable sides are 0 together). ∎
proof_key_steps: G is Lipschitz on compact subsets of D: G(B) is countably m-rectifiable, H^m(G(B ∩ K)) < ∞, and G maps H^m-null subsets of D to null sets.
bilipschitz_pieces splits B, up to a null set, into disjoint Borel pieces A_i = F_i(B_i) with F_i bi-Lipschitz on B_i and DF_i injective there.
piece_tangent, tangent_locality, piece_pullback and uniqueness give Q(F_i(b)) = range DF_i(b) for a.e. b ∈ B_i.
J := normDet D(G∘F_i)/normDet DF_i on A_i is Borel and equals the Gram Jacobian of DG along Q a.e. (Jacobian chain rule).
The injective area formula for G∘F_i and for F_i on each piece, summed over the disjoint pieces, gives the lintegral formula; the measurable embedding G|_B gives the Bochner formula.

Write D := B_{δ₁}(0) ⊆ ℝ^{n+1}, G(v) := x + ιv + u(v), DG(v) for the derivative of G at v, e_0, …, e_n for the standard basis of ℝ^{n+1}, j.succAbove for the increasing enumeration of {0, …, n} ∖ {j}, and Z₀ := {w ∈ ℝ^P : |ι*(w − x)| < δ₁/2 and |w − x − ιι*(w − x)| < δ₂}. Assume u is C¹ on D and u(v) ⊥ range ι, |u(v)| < δ₂ for every v ∈ D. Let B ⊆ D be Borel and countably n-rectifiable with H^n(B ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ D, and let ν : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^{n+1} be Borel with |ν| = 1 on B and such that, for H^n-a.e. y ∈ B, (span{ν(y)})^⊥ is the approximate tangent space of B at y. Then there are a Borel, countably n-rectifiable set M′ ⊆ Z₀ with H^n(M′) < ∞ and a map ξ′ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) that is H^n⌞M′-a.e. strongly measurable and, for H^n-a.e. w ∈ M′, a unit orientation of some subspace, such that for every n-form ω on ℝ^P with tsupport ω ⊆ Z₀: −∫_B ⟨Φ_ω(v), ν(v)⟩ dH^n(v) = ∫_{M′} ξ′(w)(ω(w)) dH^n(w), where Φ_ω(v) := Σ_{j=0}^{n} (−1)^j ω(G(v))(DG(v)e_{j.succAbove 0}, …, DG(v)e_{j.succAbove(n−1)})·e_j for v ∈ D and Φ_ω(v) := 0 for v ∉ D.

Source. Steps 3 ((**)) and 4 ((4a)–(4e)) of the supplied proof, with the De Giorgi data (B, ν) and the chart (ι, u) as hypotheses. T does not occur: the parent node codim1_rdo_local_unit_representation combines this identity with chart_divergence (T(ω) = ∫_F div Φ_ω) and de_giorgi (∫_F div Φ_ω = −∫_B⟨Φ_ω, ν⟩ dH^n). Siblings used: area_formula, normal_orientation, wedge_orientation. Departures:
(i) ξ′ is normalized by the Borel Jacobian J of area_formula, which equals J′(v) = det(⟨DG(v)σ_i, DG(v)σ_k⟩)^{1/2} of the supplied proof a.e. This makes ξ′ Borel without choosing the frames σ(v) measurably.
(ii) The area formula is applied to all of B (which is only locally finite) and restricted to B′ by an indicator.
(iii) Finiteness and rectifiability of M′ come from the first two conclusions of area_formula instead of the bound 2^{n/2}H^n(B ∩ closedBall(0, δ₁/2)).

Notation. A := ι*; π(w) := A(w − x); D′ := B_{δ₁/2}(0); B′ := B ∩ D′; H^n := μHE[n]; Q(v) := (span{ν(v)})^⊥.

1. (Chart facts.) Aι = id, and Ah = 0 iff h ⊥ range ι, since ι is an isometry. For v ∈ D: π(G(v)) = v and G(v) − x − ιπ(G(v)) = u(v), because u(v) ⊥ range ι. u maps the open set D into the closed subspace (range ι)^⊥, so every difference quotient of u, and hence every Du(v)a, lies in it; thus A∘DG(v) = A∘(ι + Du(v)) = id. Consequently G is C¹ on D, injective on D, and DG(v) is injective for v ∈ D. For v ∈ D: G(v) ∈ G(B′) iff v ∈ B′ (G injective on D).
2. (Area formula.) Apply area_formula with m := n ≥ 1, d := n + 1, the open set D, G, B and Q. Its hypotheses are step 1, B Borel with B ⊆ D, countable rectifiability, local finiteness and the a.e. tangent planes. It yields:
(R1) G(B) is countably n-rectifiable;
(R2) H^n(G(B ∩ K)) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ D;
(R3) a Borel J ≥ 0 such that, for H^n-a.e. v ∈ B and every orthonormal σ spanning Q(v), J(v) = (det[⟨DG(v)σ_i, DG(v)σ_k⟩])^{1/2};
(R4) ∫⁻_{G(B)} g dH^n = ∫⁻_B ofReal(J)·(g∘G) dH^n for all g ≥ 0;
(R5) ∫_{G(B)} f dH^n = ∫_B J·(f∘G) dH^n for all f : ℝ^P → ℝ.
3. (The set M′.) Put M′ := G(B′).
- M′ is Borel by Lusin–Souslin (B′ Borel; G continuous and injective on D).
- M′ ⊆ Z₀: for v ∈ B′, |π(G(v))| = |v| < δ₁/2 and |G(v) − x − ιπ(G(v))| = |u(v)| < δ₂.
- M′ ⊆ G(B), so M′ is countably n-rectifiable by (R1) and CountablyRectifiable.mono.
- M′ ⊆ G(B ∩ closedBall(0, δ₁/2)), and closedBall(0, δ₁/2) is a compact subset of D, so H^n(M′) < ∞ by (R2).
4. (The field ξ′.) For v ∈ ℝ^{n+1} let ξ̃(v) ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) be ξ̃(v)(α) := −Σ_j (−1)^j α(DG(v)e_{j.succAbove 0}, …, DG(v)e_{j.succAbove(n−1)})·⟨e_j, ν(v)⟩. It is linear in α and continuous (|α(b)| ≤ ‖α‖·Π_k|b_k|).
- v ↦ ξ̃(v) is Borel: v ↦ DG(v) = fderiv ℝ G v is Borel (Mathlib measurable_fderiv), ν is Borel, and b ↦ (α ↦ α(b)) is continuous.
- Define ξ′(w) := J(π(w))^{-1}·ξ̃(π(w)) for w ∈ M′ and ξ′(w) := 0 otherwise.
- ξ′ is Borel (M′ is Borel and π, J, ξ̃ are Borel), hence AE-strongly measurable for H^n⌞M′ (finite-dimensional target).
5. (Pointwise algebra.) Let V₀ ⊆ B be the set of v ∈ B at which (R3) holds; B ∖ V₀ is H^n-null. Fix v ∈ V₀. Since |ν(v)| = 1 and n ≥ 1, normal_orientation gives an orthonormal σ spanning (span{ν(v)})^⊥ = Q(v) such that β(σ) = −Σ_j (−1)^j β(e_{j.succAbove ·})⟨e_j, ν(v)⟩ for every n-covector β on ℝ^{n+1}. Put a := DG(v)∘σ : Fin n → ℝ^P. a is linearly independent, because σ is and DG(v) is injective.
(a) Applying this identity to β := α∘DG(v) gives ξ̃(v)(α) = α(a) for every n-covector α on ℝ^P.
(b) By (R3) for this σ, J(v) = (det[⟨a_i, a_k⟩])^{1/2}, which is > 0 by the first conclusion of wedge_orientation.
(c) If moreover v ∈ B′, then π(G(v)) = v and G(v) ∈ M′, so ξ′(G(v))(α) = J(v)^{-1}α(a) for all α. By the second conclusion of wedge_orientation, ξ′(G(v)) is a unit orientation of span(a).
